name: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Alarcon-Segovia Criteria (most commonly used); also Kasukawa and Sharp criteria

criteria.description: High titer anti-U1 RNP antibodies (>= 1:1600 by hemagglutination)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Alarcon-Segovia criteria: Positive anti-U1 RNP (>= 1:1600) PLUS >= 3 of 5 clinical features (hand edema, synovitis, myositis, Raynaud's, acrosclerosis). At least one of synovitis or myositis must be present.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: MCTD is sometimes considered an overlap between SLE, systemic sclerosis, and polymyositis. Some experts debate whether it is a distinct entity. Over time, patients may evolve to a more defined CTD.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Raynaud's phenomenon with high-titer anti-U1 RNP antibodies
pathognomonic.notes: Nearly universal; often the earliest symptom
Diffuse hand swelling, not localized joint swelling

occasional.notes: Especially distal esophagus; similar to scleroderma pattern
Most serious complication; leading cause of death in MCTD

rare.notes: Relatively characteristic of MCTD among CTDs
Less common than in SLE; usually membranous pattern

laboratory: High-titer anti-U1 RNP antibodies (defining serologic feature)
Anti-dsDNA usually negative or low titer
Elevated ESR and CRP during active disease
imaging: Chest CT: ground-glass opacities or fibrosis if ILD present
Echocardiography: screening for pulmonary hypertension (elevated RVSP)
Right heart catheterization for confirmed pulmonary hypertension
Hand radiographs may show erosive or non-erosive arthropathy
genetic: No specific single-gene cause; polygenic susceptibility
other: Pulmonary function tests (reduced DLCO in pulmonary hypertension/ILD)
Nailfold capillaroscopy may show dilated or dropout capillaries
EMG/nerve conduction if myositis or neuropathy suspected

distinguishingFeatures: SSc has diffuse or limited skin thickening beyond fingers
SSc has anti-Scl-70 or anti-centromere antibodies
MCTD has high-titer anti-U1 RNP as defining feature
DM has characteristic skin rashes (heliotrope, Gottron's)
DM has more prominent proximal weakness
DM has anti-Mi-2, anti-MDA5, anti-TIF1-gamma antibodies
FM lacks Raynaud's and swollen hands
FM has no objective inflammatory findings

redFlags: Progressive dyspnea on exertion (pulmonary hypertension - leading cause of death)
Declining DLCO on pulmonary function tests
Evolution of features toward a more defined CTD (SLE, SSc, polymyositis)
references: Sharp GC, et al. Mixed connective tissue disease--an apparently distinct rheumatic disease syndrome associated with a specific antibody to an extractable nuclear antigen (ENA). Am J Med. 1972;52(2):148-59.

Alarcon-Segovia D, Villarreal M. Classification and diagnostic criteria for mixed connective tissue disease. In: Kasukawa R, Sharp GC, eds. Mixed Connective Tissue Disease and Antinuclear Antibodies. 1987:33-40.
Tani C, et al. Mixed connective tissue disease: a critical appraisal. Autoimmun Rev. 2019;18(12):102448.
Gunnarsson R, et al. Mixed connective tissue disease. Best Pract Res Clin Rheumatol. 2016;30(1):95-111.
